title: O my ears
hookLine: the ears were sent to hear the truth (Anand, the ears)

lines: SO WHAT ARE THE EARS FOR?
cards: A small fact about your head: your eyes have lids. Your ears don't. You can shut out a sight in a blink, but you can't close your ears against a car alarm, a neighbor's argument, or a song you hate.
They're on duty all night, which is why an alarm clock works. Whatever is said near you goes in, wanted or not. So it matters a great deal what the ears are for.
The Anand gives them a job description.

teach.h: AE SRAVANAHU MAIRIHO: O MY EARS.
teach.b: After the body and the eyes, Guru Amar Das turns to the ears: ae sravanahu mairiho, O my ears. And he says, in paraphrase: you were sent to hear the Truth. Sent.

The word is pathaae, sent, the way a messenger is sent. The ears aren't just holes that catch whatever passes; they came with a purpose. The pauri goes on: joined to this body, listen to the true bani.
And it says what happens when they do.

teach.h: HEARING THE TRUE BANI, LIFE TURNS GREEN.
teach.b: Hearing it, mind and body become hariaa, green, the way a field in Punjab turns green after the rains, and the tongue is absorbed in its sweetness.

teach.h: NO LIDS, SO GIVE THEM SOMETHING TRUE.
teach.b: Then the pauri admits the limit: the True One is unseen and wondrous, and His state cannot be put into words.

The ears can hear the Word; they can't hear around it to the whole. It closes: hear the ambrosial Name and be made pure; you were sent to hear the Truth. A few days ago the Anand warned that hearers can be unripe.
This pauri is the other side of that coin. The same ears that soak up gossip in the break room were sent for something else. They can't close, so the pauri gives them something true to hear instead.

how: Many Sikhs recite the full Anand Sahib each morning, and many keep kirtan or recorded gurbani playing at home, at work or while driving, so the ears are filled with the Guru's word.

o: a sacred river where pilgrims bathe
a month in the Punjabi calendar
the ears, sent to hear the Truth

that line opens and closes it.
the pauri claims the ears can hear the whole of the True One

games.q: your ears can't close, and the room is full of gossip. what does the Anand say the ears are for?
o: catching everything, so nothing is missed.
hearing the Truth: they were sent for it.
nothing in particular; they just hear.
games.why: the pauri says the ears were sent, pathaae, to hear the Truth; listening to the true bani makes mind and body green.

practice: Cup your palms gently over your ears for a few breaths and notice the low hush that's left; then lift your hands and let the world back in.

Choose what the ears will hold now: a minute of kirtan or gurbani played softly, or one plain sound that's simply there, like your own breath, with no judging and no reply forming. If you pray, you can hear Waheguru once, inside.

wordCard.voice: Sravan, ear. Ae sravanahu mairiho: the Anand tells the ears they were sent to hear the Truth, and that hearing the true bani turns mind and body green.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: sravan, ear; the Anand addresses the ears as sravanahu, O ears.

carryVoice: Your line: ears, hear truth. They have no lids, but they do have a purpose. Day three hundred ninety-seven, done.

sources.ref: Ramkali M3, Anand, the ears pauri (ae sravanahu mairiho), Ang 922
